cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Test the Impossible Claim
cards.instruction: Get someone else to take the first practical step that could prove the bizarre claim true.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This tap gives you whatever you ask for. Ask for tea while I hold a cup.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're not using my good china for that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll hold a saucepan. You ask.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll ask, but I'm not tasting anything.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 directs a tap test while A holds the vessel; A3 swaps vessel and A5 requested output to keep B doing the first proving action.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 china refusal determines A3 saucepan; B4 no tasting determines A5 biscuit instead of tea.

relationship.evidence: B2 protects possessions and B4 accepts asking with a clear limit.

heightening.evidence: A5 is a modest test redesign, avoiding taste as the way to identify a liquid.

specificity.evidence: A1 alleged request-granting tap makes a visible biscuit an intelligible alternative proof.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 contains only the changed request; the tongue-as-equipment explanation was unnecessary.
